RESPO  R1: NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD.
 R2: VARINDER KUMAR
R3: ANNA  R4: ANOKH SINGH
O R D E R Heard learned counsel for the parties.

2. Leave granted.
3.

The appellant has challenged the orders dated 08.09.2022 and 05.12.2022 passed by the High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh in FAO No. 3825 of 2023 and RA-CR-138 of 2022(O&M), by which the First Appeal filed by the respondents no. 2 & 3 herein was allowed.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that he was the owner of the vehicle, which met with an accident and against which, a claim case was filed by the respondents no. 2 and 3.
5.

entities.text: High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It was submitted that the appellant had a valid insurance policy covering the vehicle and liability arising out of any accident.

The Motors Accident Claim Tribunal (for short MACT), in the claim petition, had awarded a compensation of Rs.1,50,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Fifty Thousand) with interest @9% per annum, which was enhanced to Rs.4,12,400/-(Rupees Four Lakhs Twelve Thousand Four Hundred) with interest @8% per annum.

1 6.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the liability was fastened on the appellant and the driver of the vehicle, on the ground that he did not possess a valid driving licence and thus, the insurance was unenforceable with regard to the accident, which occurred due to an unauthorized person driving the vehicle.
The appellant did not appear before the MACT and the order was ex-parte but before the High Court, the appellant appeared and also filed his cross objection.
However, the appellant, dissatisfied with the High Court's decision upholding his liability, filed a review petition which was also dismissed.

Consequently, the matter has come up before this Court for consideration.
7.

Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the licence, which was produced by the driver,
had all the requirements which indicates that it was a valid licence and acting in good faith and based on the drivers prima facie valid licence, engaged him to drive the vehicle.
It was further submitted that there was no dispute with regard to the coverage of the insurance at the time the accident occurred i.e., on 08.12.1999.

It was contended that the MACT has noticed the fact that the licence was not genuine and valid, and thus, the respondent no.1-Insurance Company, has been exonerated from any liability, which is required to be paid by the appellant and his driver.

The counsel submitted that the Courts have held that it is not expected from the owner of the vehicle to verify the licence at the time of engagement and thus, on this fact alone, a claim for insurance cannot be repudiated.

For such propositions, he has relied upon the order passed by this Court on 04.03.2020 in Nirmala Kothari Vs. United Insurance Company Ltd., (2020) 4 SCC 49 (in Civil Appeal Nos. 1999-2000 of 2020).
8.

entities.text: Nirmala Kothari Vs. United Insurance Company Ltd., (2020) 4 SCC 49
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company submitted that it was required by the appellant to lead evidence before the MACT with regard to this factual aspect, which he had not done, and thus, it cannot be presumed, in the absence of there being any factual basis before the MACT that the appellant had done due diligence before employing the driver and therefore, the judgment of this Court in Nirmala Kothari (Supra) may not be applicable in the facts of the present case.

9. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that unfortunately, he did not appear before the Tribunal but at the end of the day, the fact remains that the driver did possess a document indicating a valid and genuine driving licence and there was no reason or occasion for him to have any suspicion so as to further take an exercise of verification of the licence produced by the driver.

10. Having considered the matter, though we find that there have been laches on the part of the appellant in not appearing before the Tribunal and leading evidence with regard to the discharge of the onus on him regarding the hiring of the driver being bona fide and there being no deliberate or willful laches on his part, but for this reason, the basic factual matrix cannot be lost sight of.

At the cost of repetition, the driver did produce a licence before the appellant, which was also not disputed by the respondent no. 1, but the same on scrutiny, later before the MACT, as well as the High Court has been found to be forged and fabricated.
11.
Under these circumstances, the liability being fastened on the appellant cannot be said to be justified.

We also find that the issue is covered by the judgment of this Court in IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Geeta Devi And Ors.,
(2023) SCC OnLine SC 1398,(in SLP(C)No.19992/2023).

sentences.text: 13. For the reasons aforesaid, the appeals are partly allowed.
The respondent no.1, Insurance Company, and the respondent no.4 are held jointly responsible to satisfy the award as given by the High Court of Rs.4,12,400/- with interest @8% per annum.

14. As the respondent no. 4 has chosen not to appear, we further direct that the respondent no.1,
Insurance Company, shall pay the amount upfront and shall have the right to recover it from the respondent no. 4.
15.
If the payments have not been made, the same be made after adjusting whatever may have been paid during the interregnum, if any, within a period of two months from today.
16. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
